findings.finding: Interventional causal power can be decomposed into unique, redundant and synergistic components and can vary with context/parameters.
findings.impact: A nonzero single TOP1 cut is insufficient for broad privileged/unique responsibility language. Future H7-like work should prospectively address coalitional attribution as well as comparator adequacy.

sources: Fakhar & Hilgetag, PLoS Computational Biology 2022, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010250
Zavaglia et al., Brain Communications 2024, DOI 10.1093/braincomms/fcae251
findings.finding: Single-site/univariate lesion inference can be biased or mislocalized in interacting systems, while multi-site and multivariate methods including Multi-perturbation Shapley value Analysis perform better under synergy, redundancy and mutual inhibition in ground-truth tests.
findings.impact: Multi-site/coalitional attribution is a concrete ordinary baseline for any future distributed-responsibility claim; current H7 remains immutable.

sources: Luo et al., Nature Methods 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02654-x
findings.finding: Neural Perturbational Inference trains an ANN surrogate of system dynamics and systematically perturbs the surrogate; it was validated against generative systems with known ground-truth effective connectivity and real stimulation propagation.
findings.impact: A validated surrogate is a possible future capacity-adequate perturbational diagnostic, but prediction alone is insufficient and no current SparkBrain surrogate capability exists that fires H7's revisit trigger.

sources: Hansel & Yuste, Frontiers in Cellular Neuroscience 2024, DOI 10.3389/fncel.2024.1440588
findings.finding: The intrinsic-excitability iceberg model describes how the same previously subthreshold input can become suprathreshold without synaptic-strength change.
findings.impact: Threshold-gated latent-state separation is an ordinary mechanism class. This supports rather than weakens the ordinary reduction that killed the current Candidate #35 revisit rationale.
